Most applications will have only one Window, or
only one main window. These applications can use
Gtk::Application::make_window_and_run(int argc, char** argv, T_Args&&... args).
It creates and shows a window. When the window is closed, make_window_and_run()
deletes the window and returns to the caller.
This might happen when the user closes the window, or when your code decides to
close the window with Gtk::Window::close(). You can prevent
the user from closing the window (for instance, if there are unsaved changes) by
overriding Gtk::Window::on_close_request().
Most of our examples use this technique.
